info.description:
KasbBook's HTTP API.

The same application services the bot uses. Every permission check happens
below this layer, so an endpoint cannot be more permissive than the equivalent
button in Telegram.

Money is carried as a **string**, never a JSON number: JSON has one numeric
type and it is a float, and a bookkeeping API that loses rials is not one.
info.title: KasbBook API

delete.description:
Close the account. There is no undo, and no grace period.

Books nobody else is on go with it. Books shared with other people are not
this account's to destroy, so the request is refused until they are handed
over — `GET /auth/me/deletion-preview` names them.

post.description:
Mark it paid; with `record_transaction`, also record the money moving.

Off by default: if the original sale or purchase is already in the books,
recording the payment too counts it twice. The bot asks the same question.

delete.description: Refused once the fund has taken money — deactivate it instead.
Always safe: what past periods took is snapshotted, not recomputed.

post.description: Stop a cut taking anything after a date, without erasing what it took.

Switch a rule off or back on, without touching its dates.

This is not `close`. Off, the rule applies to no period calculated from now
on, whatever its dates say, and on again it is exactly what it was. `close`
ends the rule on a date: periods up to that date still use it, later ones
do not, and nothing here can undo it.

Switch a fund off or back on.

Flips whatever it is now, as the bot's button does; the answer says which
it became. An off fund takes nothing from any period calculated after this
and keeps its rules exactly as they were, so switching it on again restores
it. Periods that are paid or locked keep what they already took.

Record one instalment. It books an expense as well as advancing the loan.

`expected_paid_count` makes a retry safe: send the `paid_count` you last
saw, and a repeat of the same request is refused instead of paying twice.
Add someone who already has an account, by email or phone.
Hand over some or all of what is owed, in any currency the book holds.

get.description:
The receipt the bot stored, fetched from the messenger that holds it.

The receipt is the messenger's own file id, never our bytes, so this asks the provider for the
file on the person's behalf, after the usual book gate, and hands it over without keeping it.
Only a receipt held by the provider this process speaks to can be fetched; any other, and any
failure to fetch, is one answer: it is not available.
What the book holds, in the currency it holds it in.

Every currency KasbBook knows: crypto and the legal tender of every country.

The same for everyone, so it needs a sign-in but no book. Static data: a
client may keep it for a long time.

post.description: Redeem a code the messenger side produced, attaching it to this account.

get.description:
What one unit of each code is worth in `base`, across crypto, the toman and national currencies.

`exact` is false for an estimate: a national currency in toman is priced through the
dollar-pegged USDT, because no feed publishes the dollar in toman. A code nothing can price is
left out rather than guessed. With no price from either feed the answer is 503.

get.description:
Current prices, each with its source and when it was fetched.

Prices are cached in the process for about a minute, so polling this does
not become polling the provider. While the provider is down the last good
prices are returned with `stale: true` and their age; with none at all the
answer is 503.

post.description:
One update from a provider.

Always answers 200, even for an update that fails. A provider that gets an
error retries, and retrying a poisoned update forever is worse than
dropping it and logging the reason.
